asm-001.check: Lock-up restrictions on marketable equity securities not reflected in net cash judgment
asm-001.detail: Still open; the candidate is unchanged since review-01 (generator file hashes match manifest.json). Net cash (66,003M) includes marketable equity securities of 42,783M at full balance-sheet fair value. Note 5 of the 10-Q (snapshot/docs/periodic.txt line 792, footnote (1) to the Jul 26, 2026 table) says $36.9B of these investments are subject to short-term lock-up restrictions on the ability to sell. The mapping rationale says 'the valuation step may haircut them', but valuation_inputs.json applies no haircut and its rationales do not discuss the point. note.md (Net cash paragraph) mentions fair-value volatility but not the lock-up. Re-computed impact: excluding the full $36.9B lowers both the DCF and the peer per-share values by about $1.52/share, so the blended value falls from $186.14 to about $184.6 (upside about -12.0%). The rating stays Underperform, so the conclusion does not change. This corrects review-01's estimate of about $1.2. The restriction should still be disclosed.
asm-001.required_evidence: note.md net-cash judgment (or valuation_inputs rationale) mentions that about $36.9B of marketable equity is under short-term lock-up and states whether a haircut is applied

cmp-001.check: Code-generated disclosure attributes all figures to SEC XBRL, but the share price and peer prices come from the Yahoo price snapshot
cmp-001.detail: Still open; the candidate has not changed since review-01 (generator/note.md sha256 231445d2...1764 matches manifest.json, and all recompute hashes match gates.json). The final Disclosures bullet still reads 'All figures in this note are generated by code from SEC XBRL data (and, for guidance, taken from verbatim filing quotes) and are unaudited by the author.' The last close ($209.66), the upside (-11.3%), the peer median EV/Sales (23.0x) and the target price depend on snapshot/prices.json and snapshot/peers.json (Yahoo chart-endpoint closes dated 2026-08-26), not on XBRL. The data-source bullet does name the Yahoo price snapshot, so provenance is not hidden; the blanket statement is just broader than the facts. Suggested wording: 'generated by code from SEC XBRL data and the case price snapshot'.
cmp-001.required_evidence: The disclosure names both SEC XBRL and the price snapshot as the sources of code-generated figures

prov-001.check: Forecast prose says opex grows more slowly than revenue; assumptions do not show that across the horizon
prov-001.detail: Still open: the candidate is unchanged (note.md sha256 231445d2..., assumptions.json sha256 d48689ee... match manifest and review-01). note.md (Guidance and outlook, Judgment) still says the model lets operating expenses grow more slowly than revenue after FY2027Q3. assumptions.json opex_pct_revenue runs 0.0852, 0.0844, 0.0844, 0.0852. Recomputed from forecast.json: opex 9.201bn -> 10.027bn (+9.0%) -> 10.829bn (+8.0%) -> 11.697bn (+8.0%) against revenue +10%, +8%, +7%. Opex grows more slowly than revenue only in FY2027Q4, at the same rate in FY2028Q1 and faster in FY2028Q2, and the exit ratio equals the starting ratio. The numbers are correct, but the sentence overstates the operating leverage assumed.
prov-001.required_evidence: Sentence describes opex as roughly constant at about 8.4-8.5% of revenue, or assumptions changed to match the prose
